ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Alice is standing on the circumference of a large circular room of radius $10$. There is a circular pillar in the center of the room of radius $5$ that blocks Alice's view. The total area in the room Alice can see can be expressed in the form $\frac{m\pi}{n} +p\sqrt{q}$, where $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime positive integers and $p$ and $q$ are integers such that $q$ is square-free. Compute $m + n + p + q$. (Note that the pillar is not included in the total area of the room.)\n<image1>

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a large circle representing a room with radius 10, and a concentric small circle representing a central pillar with radius 5; Alice is located at point A on the circumference at the bottom of the large circle; from A, draw two tangents to the small circle and extend them to the large circle, forming left-right symmetric boundary lines, and the blocked region is bounded by these tangents and the upper outer circular arc. Reasoning: Let the common center of the large circle and the pillar be O, draw a tangent from Alice's position A to the pillar, let the tangent point be T, and let the tangent intersect the outer circle again at B and C. In right triangle AOT, AO=10, OT=5, and OT is perpendicular to AT, so cos∠AOT=OT/AO=1/2, obtaining ∠AOT=60°. The two tangents are symmetric, therefore the corresponding central angle on the upper part of the outer circle ∠BOC=120°. Chord BC=2·10·sin60°=10√3, and the distance from BC to O is 10cos60°=5, so the height from A to BC is 10+5=15. Thus the area of triangle ABC is (1/2)(10√3)(15)=75√3. The area of the circular segment above chord BC equals the sector area with radius 10 and central angle 120° minus the area of triangle OBC, namely 100π/3 - (1/2)(10)(10)sin120° = 100π/3 - 25√3. Therefore the invisible shadow area containing the pillar is 75√3 + 100π/3 - 25√3 = 100π/3 + 50√3. The visible room area does not include the pillar, and this shadow already includes the pillar, so the visible area is the outer circle area minus this shadow: 100π - (100π/3 + 50√3)=200π/3 - 50√3. Therefore m=200, n=3, p=-50, q=3, and the requested m+n+p+q=200+3-50+3=156.

method.method_draft: Use a synthetic geometry decomposition of the tangent-bounded shadow. Let O be the common center, A Alice's point on the outer circle, and draw the two tangents from A to the central pillar, meeting the outer circle again at B and C. From right triangle AOT, where T is a tangent point, AO=10 and OT=5, so the relevant central angle is 120 degrees. The unseen shadow including the pillar is the region bounded by chords AB, AC and the outer arc BC. Decompose this shadow into triangle ABC plus the circular segment over chord BC: triangle ABC has base BC=10sqrt(3) and height 15, so area 75sqrt(3); the segment is the 120-degree sector of radius 10 minus triangle OBC, giving 100pi/3-25sqrt(3). Thus the shadow including the pillar has area 100pi/3+50sqrt(3). Since this shadow contains the pillar, the visible room area excluding the pillar is simply outer disk area minus this shadow: 100pi-(100pi/3+50sqrt(3))=200pi/3-50sqrt(3). Therefore m=200, n=3, p=-50, q=3, and the requested sum is 156.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates and integrate the shadow region. Place the center of the room at O=(0,0) and Alice at A=(0,-10). A tangent line from A to the pillar x^2+y^2=25 has equation y=sqrt(3)x-10 on the right and y=-sqrt(3)x-10 on the left; these meet the outer circle x^2+y^2=100 at x=±5sqrt(3), y=5. The shadow including the pillar is the part of the outer disk between these tangent rays, so its area is 2 times the integral from x=0 to 5sqrt(3) of the vertical difference between the outer circle y=sqrt(100-x^2) and the tangent line y=sqrt(3)x-10. Thus compute 2∫_0^{5sqrt(3)} [sqrt(100-x^2)-sqrt(3)x+10] dx. Evaluating with the standard antiderivative for sqrt(100-x^2) gives shadow area 100pi/3+50sqrt(3). The visible non-pillar area equals outer disk area minus this full shadow, since the pillar lies entirely inside it: 100pi-(100pi/3+50sqrt(3))=200pi/3-50sqrt(3). Hence m=200, n=3, p=-50, q=3, giving m+n+p+q=156.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是一个半径为10的大圆形房间，中心有半径为5的圆形柱子，Alice 位于大圆底部圆周点 A。两条视线从 A 向柱子作切线，并继续延伸到外圆，形成柱子后方不可见的阴影区域。推理：按指定方法设房间中心 O=(0,0)，Alice 在 A=(0,-10)。右侧从 A 到柱子 x^2+y^2=25 的切线为 y=sqrt(3)x-10，左侧为 y=-sqrt(3)x-10。右侧切线与外圆 x^2+y^2=100 相交时，代入得 x^2+(sqrt(3)x-10)^2=100，所以 4x^2-20sqrt(3)x=0，非零交点为 x=5sqrt(3)，此时 y=5。由对称性，阴影区域（按方法草稿，包含柱子）面积为 2∫_0^(5sqrt(3)) [sqrt(100-x^2)-sqrt(3)x+10] dx。使用 ∫sqrt(100-x^2)dx = (x/2)sqrt(100-x^2)+50arcsin(x/10)。在 x=5sqrt(3) 时，sqrt(100-x^2)=5，arcsin(sqrt(3)/2)=pi/3，所以该部分积分为 25sqrt(3)/2+50pi/3。其余部分 ∫_0^(5sqrt(3))(-sqrt(3)x+10)dx = -75sqrt(3)/2+50sqrt(3)=25sqrt(3)/2。因此右半阴影面积为 50pi/3+25sqrt(3)，总阴影面积为 100pi/3+50sqrt(3)。外圆面积为 100pi，所以可见且不包括柱子的面积为 100pi-(100pi/3+50sqrt(3))=200pi/3-50sqrt(3)。因此 m=200，n=3，p=-50，q=3，m+n+p+q=200+3-50+3=156。

推理：设房间中心 O=(0,0)，Alice 在 A=(0,-10)，外圆为 x^2+y^2=100，柱子为 x^2+y^2=25。右侧从 A 到柱子的切线可写为 y=√3x-10，左侧为 y=-√3x-10。将右侧切线与外圆联立：x^2+(√3x-10)^2=100，化简得 4x^2-20√3x=0，所以非零交点为 x=5√3，此时 y=5。

raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a large circle representing a room with radius 10, and a concentric small circle representing a central pillar with radius 5; Alice is located at point A on the circumference at the bottom of the large circle; from A, draw two tangents to the small circle and extend them to the large circle, forming left-right symmetric boundary lines, and the blocked region is bounded by these tangents and the upper outer circular arc. Reasoning: Let the common center of the large circle and the pillar be O, draw a tangent from Alice's position A to the pillar, let the tangent point be T, and let the tangent intersect the outer circle again at B and C. In right triangle AOT, AO=10, OT=5, and OT is perpendicular to AT, so cos∠AOT=OT/AO=1/2, obtaining ∠AOT=60°. The two tangents are symmetric, therefore the corresponding central angle on the upper part of the outer circle ∠BOC=120°. Therefore the invisible shadow area containing the pillar is 75√3 + 100π/3 - 25√3 = 100π/3 + 50√3. The visible room area does not include the pillar, and this shadow already includes the pillar, so the visible area is the outer circle area minus this shadow: 100π - (100π/3 + 50√3)=200π/3 - 50√3. Therefore m=200, n=3, p=-50, q=3, and the requested m+n+p+q=200+3-50+3=156.
